efe55e142333.title: Releasing the libraries
efe55e142333.content: How an agent publishes the HCERT libraries (STT-NFR-002) once the owner has supplied credentials. Nothing is published yet. No GitHub workflow publishes and no workflow holds a credential: CI runs only the dry runs below, in the check, kotlin and rust jobs of .github/workflows/requirements-kg.yml. An agent runs the commands here, from a clean checkout of the release tag, and stops at the first failure.

6da6be490883.title: What is published
6da6be490883.content: One version for all of them, from VERSION (STT-NFR-001), with an entry in CHANGELOG.md that cites each smart-trust changes.md entry it implements. | Registry | Coordinates | Built by | . | Maven Central | io.github.litlfred:hcert-api, io.github.litlfred:hcert-core (Kotlin Multiplatform: the root module, plus -jvm and -js) | gradle -p tools/hcert-kotlin publishDryRun | . | crates.io | litlfred-hcert (library name hcert) | cargo package in tools/hcert-rust | . | npm | @litlfred/hcert-kotlin-js (Kotlin/JS ES module) | tools/release-packaging/assemble-npm.mjs | . | npm | @litlfred/hcert-component (the Rust WebAssembly component, transpiled with jco) | tools/hcert-rust/build-component.sh, then assemble-npm.mjs | . The coordinates follow the repository’s GitHub org (the owner’s decision of 2026-10-23). Their single source is "repository": "<org>/<name>" in smart-trust-tools.json: the Maven group is io.github.<org> (a namespace the org can verify on the Sonatype Central Portal through GitHub), the npm scope is @<org>, and the crate is <org>-hcert, because crates.io has no namespaces (the Rust library itself stays hcert). The Gradle build and tools/release-packaging/coordinates.mjs derive them; check-version.mjs fails if Cargo.toml, a POM or a package.json disagrees. Moving the repository to another org (say, WorldHealthOrganization) means changing that one field, renaming the crate in Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock as the check asks, and verifying the new namespaces below. The Kotlin package root stays who.smart.trust. Android uses the -jvm jar as it is; there is no AAR until an androidTarget() exists.

9df578801d06.title: Once, before the first release
9df578801d06.content: . | Licence. Apache-2.0 (the owner’s decision of 2026-10-23; OI-14). LICENSE is the official text from apache.org (sha256 cfc7749b…3d30); the crate ships its copy tools/hcert-rust/LICENSE (the check requires it to be identical), assemble-npm.mjs copies it into each npm package, and every jar carries it as META-INF/LICENSE. | Maven Central. Sign in to https://central.sonatype.com with the litlfred GitHub account; the io.github.litlfred namespace is verified by that. Generate a user token (View Account → Generate User Token): it is a name and a password, CENTRAL_TOKEN_USER and CENTRAL_TOKEN_PASS below. | Signing key. Central requires an OpenPGP signature on every file. Generate a key for releases, then publish its public half: gpg --quick-gen-key "Carl Leitner (smart-trust-tools releases)" ed25519 sign 2y gpg --list-secret-keys --keyid-format long # note the key id, KEYID below gpg --keyserver keys.openpgp.org --send-keys KEYID gpg --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com --send-keys KEYID . The key stays on the owner’s machine (or a hardware token). No key, token or passphrase is ever committed or given to a workflow. | crates.io. Sign in with GitHub at https://crates.io, verify an e-mail address, and create an API token scoped to publish-new and publish-update for the crate litlfred-hcert (CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN). | npm. The packages are scoped to the npm user litlfred. Create a granular access token with read and write on @litlfred/* (NPM_TOKEN), with two-factor authentication on the account. | .

5bd38ead12ae.title: Pre-release checks
5bd38ead12ae.content: From the repository root, on main, with a clean tree: . git status --porcelain # must print nothing git log -1 --format=%H origin/main # must equal HEAD; CI green on it cat VERSION # the version to release, no pre-release suffix . | Set the version, if it changes, in the three places that hold it, then let Cargo update its own entry in the lock (no other crate moves): echo 0.1.0 > VERSION sed -i 's/^version = ".*"/version = "0.1.0"/' tools/hcert-rust/Cargo.toml # the [package] version, the only line it matches (cd tools/hcert-rust && cargo update --workspace --offline) . | In CHANGELOG.md, replace — unreleased in the version’s heading with the date (## [0.1.0] — 2026-11-02), make sure every wire-format or subclaim-default change cites its smart-trust changes.md entry, and point the link at the tag ([0.1.0]: https://github.com/litlfred/smart-trust-tools/releases/tag/v0.1.0). A wire-format or subclaim-default change needs a major or minor bump. | Run the checks CI runs, and the dry runs: node tools/release-packaging/check-version.mjs bun run check:req-nodes python3 tools/test-plan/make_test_plan.py --check python3 tools/wit2kotlin/wit2kotlin.py --check gradle -p tools/hcert-kotlin --no-daemon compileKotlinJvm compileKotlinJs :hcert-core:jvmTest :hcert-core:jvmTestCoverageCheck :hcert-core:compileProductionLibraryKotlinJs (cd tools/hcert-rust && cargo test --locked && cargo test --locked --features qr --test api) . | Commit (Release 0.1.0), push to main of litlfred/smart-trust-tools, wait for CI to pass on that commit, then tag it with a signed tag and push the tag: git tag -s v0.1.0 -m "smart-trust-tools 0.1.0" git push origin v0.1.0 . | . Every artefact is then built from a fresh clone of the tag, never from a working copy: . git clone --branch v0.1.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/litlfred/smart-trust-tools.git /tmp/stt-release cd /tmp/stt-release bun run cat mount:lock && bun install # the mounted layers, for check:req-nodes . toolchain/node_tools.sh # jco, from the lockfile, no install scripts .

f9236a8aa92f.title: Maven Central (Central Portal bundle upload)
f9236a8aa92f.content: . | Publish into the build-local repository and check the result. Every archive is reproducible (no timestamps, fixed order), so building the tag twice from a fresh clone gives the same jars, klibs, sources jars and POMs. The Kotlin Gradle plugin (2.0.21) writes the org.gradle.libraryelements attribute into hcert-api’s .module files or not depending on which tasks the build runs, so run exactly this command: gradle -p tools/hcert-kotlin --no-daemon publishDryRun node tools/release-packaging/check-version.mjs tools/hcert-kotlin/build/maven-dry-run . publishDryRun lists, for each of hcert-api, hcert-api-jvm, hcert-api-js, hcert-core, hcert-core-jvm and hcert-core-js: the .pom, the .module (Gradle metadata), the main artefact (.jar, or .klib for -js), -sources.jar, -javadoc.jar (the module README; the KDoc is in the sources) and, for the root modules, -kotlin-tooling-metadata.json. Gradle writes .md5, .sha1, .sha256 and .sha512 beside each. | Sign every artefact (not the checksums, not maven-metadata.xml): repo=tools/hcert-kotlin/build/maven-dry-run find "$repo" -name 'maven-metadata.xml*' -delete find "$repo" -type f ! -name '*.md5' ! -name '*.sha1' ! -name '*.sha256' ! -name '*.sha512' \ -exec gpg --local-user KEYID --armor --detach-sign {} \; find "$repo" -name '*.asc' -exec gpg --verify {} \; . | Bundle the repository layout and upload it, as a deployment the owner releases by hand (USER_MANAGED): (cd "$repo" && zip -qrX ../central-bundle-0.1.0.zip io) token=$(printf '%s:%s' "$CENTRAL_TOKEN_USER" "$CENTRAL_TOKEN_PASS" | base64 -w0) curl --fail --request POST \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $token" \ --form bundle=@tools/hcert-kotlin/build/central-bundle-0.1.0.zip \ "https://central.sonatype.com/api/v1/publisher/upload?name=smart-trust-hcert-0.1.0&publishingType=USER_MANAGED" # prints the deployment id curl --fail --request POST --header "Authorization: Bearer $token" \ "https://central.sonatype.com/api/v1/publisher/status?id=DEPLOYMENT_ID" . Wait for "deploymentState": "VALIDATED"; on FAILED, the response lists each problem. Then release it, which cannot be undone: . curl --fail --request POST --header "Authorization: Bearer $token" \ "https://central.sonatype.com/api/v1/publisher/deployment/DEPLOYMENT_ID" . (or Publish on the deployment at https://central.sonatype.com/publishing/deployments). | .

c67c1d87e0c3.title: crates.io
c67c1d87e0c3.content: cd tools/hcert-rust cargo package --locked --list # exactly: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, README.md, DEPENDENCIES.md, LICENSE, src/*.rs cargo package --locked # builds the .crate on its own, from target/package/litlfred-hcert-0.1.0 cargo publish --locked --dry-run CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN=... cargo publish --locked . The tests are not in the crate: they read the shared vectors at ../../vectors, so they run from the repository. The component feature reads the WIT contract at ../../api/wit and so builds only from the repository too; the component is published to npm instead. A crates.io version cannot be replaced, only yanked (cargo yank --version 0.1.0).

2de0894e3c26.title: npm
2de0894e3c26.content: tools/hcert-rust/build-component.sh /tmp/stt-component gradle -p tools/hcert-kotlin --no-daemon :hcert-core:compileProductionLibraryKotlinJs node tools/release-packaging/assemble-npm.mjs --out /tmp/stt-npm \ --component /tmp/stt-component \ --kotlin-js tools/hcert-kotlin/hcert-core/build/compileSync/js/main/productionLibrary/kotlin node tools/release-packaging/check-version.mjs /tmp/stt-npm node tools/conformance-ts/run.mjs rust /tmp/stt-npm/hcert-component # the shipped files pass the suite node tools/conformance-ts/run.mjs kotlin /tmp/stt-npm/hcert-kotlin-js for p in hcert-component hcert-kotlin-js; do (cd /tmp/stt-npm/$p && npm pack --ignore-scripts --pack-destination /tmp/stt-npm) done sha256sum /tmp/stt-npm/*.tgz # record in the release notes . Then publish the tarballs that were checked, not the directories (scoped packages are private unless --access public): . printf '//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=%s\n' "$NPM_TOKEN" > /tmp/stt-npmrc npm publish /tmp/stt-npm/litlfred-hcert-component-0.1.0.tgz --access public --ignore-scripts --userconfig /tmp/stt-npmrc --otp=CODE npm publish /tmp/stt-npm/litlfred-hcert-kotlin-js-0.1.0.tgz --access public --ignore-scripts --userconfig /tmp/stt-npmrc --otp=CODE rm /tmp/stt-npmrc . An npm version cannot be republished once used, even after npm unpublish.

792e697fad7c.title: After publishing
792e697fad7c.content: . | Check that each coordinate resolves to the release (the STT-NFR-002 success criterion): curl -sI https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/io/github/litlfred/hcert-core-jvm/0.1.0/hcert-core-jvm-0.1.0.pom | head -1 curl -s https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/litlfred-hcert/0.1.0 | head -c 200 npm view @litlfred/hcert-component@0.1.0 version npm view @litlfred/hcert-kotlin-js@0.1.0 version . 8a5edab28263.title: SMART Trust HCERT library tools
8a5edab28263.content: Requirements and contracts for the SMART Trust HCERT API libraries: Kotlin first (JVM, Android, Node), Rust second (WebAssembly). They are derived from the WHO SMART Trust implementation guide, in particular the QR Code Generation page of WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust#129.

47442bd40ecb.title: Viewers
47442bd40ecb.content: | Viewer | What it shows | . | Overview | The viewers’ own landing page, with counts and the pipeline | . | Graph explorer | The requirements knowledge graph, grouped and drillable | . | Traceability matrix | Every requirement against its sources, skills, contract items (WIT, CDDL) and open issues | . | Requirements | The library requirements (cat-harness req: nodes), each with every edge of the graph | . | API contract | The library API in WIT, with its TypeScript reference | . | Wire and payload models | CDDL wire format; JSON-LD, SHACL and CDDL from the FHIR logical models | . | Kotlin skeleton | The Kotlin Multiplatform API generated from the WIT | . | Node kinds | Which cat-harness nodes the graph is read from, and the field each edge comes from | . | User journeys | What the library does for each step of journeys J1 to J4, and the gaps | .

df7b2e9a0e1a.title: Sources
df7b2e9a0e1a.content: Every part of the graph is a cat-harness node of this instance: . | requirements: skills/requirements/, one req: node per STT-<AREA>-nnn, each citing what it is drawn from in reference; | what they cite: library/ (WHO SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw and IHE ITI VHL, section by section at pinned commits), external-schemas/, references/ and memory/; | what realizes them: the skills in skills/, the Tools in tools/ (the Kotlin library is tools/hcert-kotlin/), and the processes in processes/content/; | open issues: the beans in beans/defs/. | .

356e2419c4b9.title: User journey coverage (DRAFT journeys J1 to J4)
356e2419c4b9.content: What the HCERT library must do for each step of the workshop storyline, and whether it does. OHS Player, OHS Stack and the CHW and wallet apps are consumers of the Kotlin library; rendering, scanning, storage, HTTP and FHIR record keeping are theirs. Source: stakeholder directive dir-journeys, 2026-10-20. | Journey step | Library capability | Status | . | J1 Country A clinic issues a DVC for each newborn vaccine (Hep B, polio) | DVCMin payload, one event per certificate (STT-PAY-003); no identity document for a newborn (STT-PAY-005); guardian name gn; any national vaccine code in vp (extensible binding) | Done: HcertIssuer.prepare / finish | . | J1 signs with the clinic’s DSC key held in Android Keystore or an HSM | Two-phase signing, no private key in process (STT-ISS-004, STT-COS-006) | Done | . | J1 printed paper QR, or SMS/MMS | HC1 string is QR Alphanumeric only (STT-QR-001); the app renders it at error correction Q | Done (rendering is the app’s) | . | J1 DEV keys and DEV trust list | Trust store loads GDHCN DID trustlist v2 documents (DEV, UAT, PROD alike) and PEM | Done: addDidDocument, addPem; the app fetches from the trust list distribution endpoints | . | J2 CHW, offline, reads the foreign QR to register the child and refer | Explicitly named unverified read, its result typed as unverified (STT-VER-011) | Done: HcertVerifier.readUnverified | . | J2 alternative: verify offline on the CHW device | Verification is synchronous and offline against a store the app filled earlier (STT-GEN-012, STT-VER-009) | Done; which one J2 uses is the journey’s open question | . | J3 Clinic verifies the foreign DVC | GDHCN verification in the STT-VER-001 order, typed failures (STT-VER-008), EKU check (STT-VER-004) | Done: HcertVerifier.verify, PR 129 vector verifies on JVM and Node | . | J3 imports the immunization into the domestic record | The verified DVCMin fields; mapping to FHIR R4 Immunization/Patient | Not in this library (the app maps). Worked examples in smart-trust-demo: TrustDemoJ3HepB and TrustDemoJ3Bcg, with their verification provenance | . | J3 adds the national schedule code beside the foreign vaccine code | The library passes the issuer’s vp code through unchanged and rejects nothing for an unknown code. The translation is a FHIR ConceptMap ($translate) the clinic EHR applies, adding the national coding and never replacing the issuer’s | Not in this library. Worked example in smart-trust-demo: ConceptMap TrustDemoProductToOnesaEpi (product → national schedule dose of Onesa, the demo’s fictional home country); a product with no entry goes to the nurse, whose decision is recorded (TrustDemoJ3Adjudication) and added to the map | . | J4.0 National portal issues one passcode-protected VHL QR per family member | VHL payload (SHL payload format, flag P) as a CBOR map at HCERT claim -260 key 5 (STT-VHL-001, STT-VHL-002); key generation (STT-VHL-004); JWE dir / A256GCM encryption of each document (STT-VHL-007) | Done: HcertIssuer with Payload.Vhl, HcertVhl.newKey, HcertVhl.encrypt; hosting the manifest and enforcing the passcode are the VHL host’s | . | J4.1 Clinic abroad scans a VHL, fetches with passcode, reads IPS | Verify the VHL HCERT, map or vhlink:/ string at key 5, and the link’s exp (STT-VHL-002, STT-VHL-009); ITI-YY5 request (STT-VHL-005); HTTP Message Signatures (STT-VHL-008); manifest Bundle (STT-VHL-006); decrypt each document (STT-VHL-007) | Done: HcertVerifier.verify, HcertVhl.buildManifestRequest, buildSignatureBase/signatureHeader, parseManifest, decrypt; the HTTP, mutual TLS and AuditEvents are the app’s | .

0f7e265c1b9d.title: VHL: what the specifications say, and where they disagree
0f7e265c1b9d.content: Changes raised upstream: WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust#130 (subclaim 5 is a VHL, a CBOR map), WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust-phw#17 (payload types match SMART Health Links), and a patch for IHE ITI.VHL in upstream/ihe-iti-vhl/ (ITI-YY3 key 5 as a CBOR map, example fixes). Open issues OI-21 to OI-29. The IHE ITI VHL profile and the WHO VerifiableHealthLinkPayload model share the SMART Health Links payload fields, but: . | IHE’s manifest is a FHIR List search returning a searchset Bundle of DocumentReferences (ITI-YY5), not the SMART Health Links files[] manifest; the Bundle is not signed, and the journey’s “signed VHL manifests” exist in neither specification. | The value at hcert key 5 is a vhlink:/ text string in ITI-YY3 but a decoded JSON object in the ITI-YY4 example; HCERT 3.2.7.1.5 calls it a SMART Health Link (OI-06). | WHO requires type (vhl) and types exp and v as strings; IHE has no type and uses numbers. | JWE alg/enc are not normative (the example is dir / A256GCM); no zip. | Requester authentication (RFC 9421 HTTP signatures, UDAP, or a VC) and the DID trust list’s mapping to a COSE kid are under-specified. | .
